Patrick Witt: The U.S. Government Needs Explicit Congressional Authorization to Legally Buy Bitcoin

On November 10, 2026, Patrick Witt, former executive director of the White House Crypto Council, said in an interview with What Bitcoin Did that President Donald Trump is interested in adding to the government's Bitcoin holdings. The administration has discussed several ways to do so, but legal questions remain over whether the government can buy Bitcoin directly on the open market and how it could do so without triggering a negative market reaction.

Witt said the administration wants to codify the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and secure explicit authorization from Congress. Because Congress controls appropriations, the administration would have to show that buying Bitcoin falls within the original purpose of any existing funds it plans to use. He added that moving prematurely could prompt Congress to insert a provision into the National Defense Authorization Act banning such purchases, undermining efforts to secure authorization. — link

Vitalik on EIP-8037: Curb State Growth to Scale Ethereum, Recommends Clarifying Future Protocol Changes

Vitalik Buterin said EIP-8037 raises gas costs for creating storage slots, code and accounts to decouple execution scaling from state growth while preserving security. He estimates that a 10x gas limit increase alongside Glamsterdam proposals excluding EIP-8037 would raise annual state growth from roughly 110 GiB to 1,100 GiB. Most core developers currently favor helping applications fix compatibility issues before Glamsterdam, which has been delayed. He also urged clearer communication of potential changes to gas mechanics, state trees, blob structures, consensus and transaction formats, noting that the consensus algorithm could change substantially over the next two years and older transaction types may eventually be retired. — link

64,000 Bitcoin Mining Machines Hijacked, Redirecting 13 EH/s to OCEAN Pool

Bitcoin News reported that approximately 64,000 Bitcoin mining machines, representing about 13 EH/s of hashrate, were hijacked around 20:00 U.S. Central Time on November 14. The attackers redirected the hashrate to OCEAN and replaced the mining payout address with one they controlled, briefly pushing the pool's hashrate close to 50 EH/s.

CoreX Hosting said the incident appeared to have ended on November 15, with the affected hashrate falling to around 100 PH/s. The attackers failed to mine any blocks and received no block rewards, although affected miners lost mining revenue during the incident. A potential compromise of Luxor Commander software has not been independently confirmed. — link
